extracted.intended_audience: agency rulewriters, OIRA/OMB staff, administrative lawyers, policy analysts, regulatory affairs professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A compendium summarizing Executive Office of the President (EOP) Executive Orders, Bulletins, and Memoranda that impose procedural and substantive requirements on federal agency rulemaking, including OIRA review, cost-benefit analysis, public participation, retrospective review, and other regulatory policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 12630 — Governmental Actions and Interference with Constitutionally Protected Property Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency 'shall be guided by' the principles set forth in the EO when 'formulating or implementing policies that have takings implications.' Agencies are required, to the extent permitted by law, to comply with a set of criteria before undertaking covered actions that include an assessment identifying the risk, establishing that safety is substantially advanced and that restrictions are not disproportionate to the overall risk, and estimating the cost to the government if the action is found to be a taking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles include that the mere assertion of a safety purpose is insufficient to avoid a taking; measures should address real and substantial threats, significantly advance safety, and be no greater than necessary. Policies that may have takings implications include proposed and final rules that 'could effect a taking' (e.g., licenses, permits, or other conditions or limitations on private property use). OMB and DOJ are responsible for ensuring compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 12866 — Regulatory Planning and Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires agencies to identify 'significant regulatory actions' and submit such actions to OIRA for review; retains requirement that 'economically significant' rules (generally $100 million annual effect) be accompanied by cost-benefit assessments when forwarded to OIRA as proposed and final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant regulatory actions include those with material adverse effects on the economy, sectors, productivity, competition, jobs, environment, public health or safety, or governments; those that may materially alter budgetary impact of benefit programs or rights of recipients; those raising novel legal or policy issues; or those inconsistent with other agency actions. The EO establishes transparency (public availability of submissions to OIRA and changes made at OIRA's behest), a 90-day OIRA review deadline (plus one 30-day extension), and a process for resolving disputes (Vice President decision/recommendation). It also establishes annual Regulatory Plans and continued publication of the Unified Agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 12889 — Implementation of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies subject to the APA must provide at least a 75-day comment period for 'any proposed Federal technical regulation or any Federal sanitary or phytosanitary measure of general application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include regulations implementing NAFTA on its effective date, technical regulations relating to perishable goods, urgent safety/protection rules, and urgent sanitary or phytosanitary protection. The EO defines 'technical regulations' and 'sanitary or phytosanitary measures' consistent with the Trade Agreements Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 12988 — Civil Justice Reform (regulatory drafting standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must review existing and new regulations to ensure they 'eliminate drafting errors and ambiguity' and 'provide a clear legal standard for affected conduct rather than a general standard,' and to make every reasonable effort to meet specified objectives (e.g., specify preemptive or retroactive effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must determine that the rule meets the applicable standards or document why it is unreasonable to meet one or more standards. This is intended to improve regulatory drafting to reduce needless litigation. The EO applies to agencies as defined in law (see Section 105 of title 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13045 — Protection of Children from Environmental Health Risks and Safety Risks
rubrics_metrics.description: For any substantive rulemaking action that 'is likely to result in' an economically significant rule concerning environmental health or safety risks that may disproportionately affect children, agencies must provide OMB/OIRA an evaluation of the effects on children and an explanation of why the planned regulation is preferable to other effective and reasonably feasible alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy calls on agencies to 'address disproportionate risks to children' to the extent permitted by law and appropriate. Agencies must evaluate environmental health or safety effects attributable to products/substances children are likely to contact or ingest, and explain alternatives considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13132 — Federalism considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires agencies to consider federalism implications and consult with state/local officials as set out in the EO when developing rules that have federalism implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references a detailed table (13132 table) summarizing requirements; agencies must follow consultation and coordination procedures specified in the EO.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13175 — Consultation and Coordination with Indian Tribal Governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs agencies to consult and coordinate with Indian Tribal Governments as specified in the EO when agency actions have tribal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the EO's table for further specifics; the EO includes procedural requirements for tribal consultation and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13211 — Actions Concerning Regulations That Significantly Affect Energy Supply, Distribution, or Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must prepare and submit to OIRA a Statement of Energy Effects for significant energy actions, describing any adverse effects on energy supply, distribution, or use and reasonable alternatives and their effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'significant energy action' is one that is 'significant' under EO 12866 and likely to have a significant adverse energy effect, or designated as such by the OIRA Administrator. Agencies must publish the Statement or a summary in the related NPRM and final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13272 — Proper Consideration of Small Entities in Agency Rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must notify the Small Business Administration's Office of Advocacy (Advocacy) of draft rules that may have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities when the draft rule is submitted to OIRA (or at a reasonable time prior to publication if not submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must give 'every appropriate consideration' to Advocacy comments and, where consistent with legal requirements, include responses to Advocacy comments in final rule preambles unless the agency head certifies the public interest is not served. Agencies must issue written procedures to ensure potential impacts on small businesses, small governmental jurisdictions, and small organizations are properly considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13563 — Improving Regulation and Regulatory Review (supplement to EO 12866)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must ensure that benefits of rulemaking justify costs, tailor regulations to impose the least burden, consider cumulative burdens, maximize net benefits, use performance objectives, assess available alternatives, provide meaningful public comment opportunities (generally 60 days), timely and easy internet access to pertinent documents, consider views of those likely to be affected prior to NPRMs when feasible, promote coordination/simplification/harmonization, consider flexible approaches, ensure objectivity of scientific/technological information, and promote retrospective analysis with a plan to periodically review significant regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public participation: 'meaningful opportunity' for comment and easy access to all pertinent documents. Integration and innovation: coordination across agencies to reduce redundancy and promote innovation. Flexible approaches: consider approaches that reduce burdens and maintain flexibility and freedom of choice. Objectivity: ensure objectivity of scientific information/processes supporting rulemaking. Retrospective analysis: agencies must have a plan to periodically review significant regulations to make them more effective or less burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13579 — Regulation and Independent Regulatory Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourages independent regulatory agencies to promote EO 13563 goals and conduct retrospective analyses of rules to determine if they are outmoded, ineffective, insufficient, or excessively burdensome; publish analyses online when possible and develop a plan within 120 days to periodically review regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EO is specifically geared toward independent agencies and asks them to publish analyses and adopt periodic review plans similar to EO 13563's expectations for executive agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13609 — Promoting International Regulatory Cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires agencies to include in their Regulatory Plan a summary of international regulatory cooperation activities (if required to submit a plan), designate regulations with international impacts in the Unified Agenda and on public sites, and consider reforming significant regulations that create unnecessary differences between U.S. and international systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consider regulatory approaches abroad and any regulatory cooperation obligations under work plans; designate international-impact regulations in the Unified Agenda, regulations.gov, and reginfo.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13610 — Identifying and Reducing Regulatory Burdens (retrospective review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are instructed to institutionalize regular reviews of previously issued significant regulations and increase public participation in retrospective review; agencies must report on the status of retrospective review efforts to OIRA regularly (on the second Monday of January and July), and make final reports available to the public within three weeks of submission of draft reports to OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should contain progress on review, anticipated accomplishments, and proposed timelines; regular reporting cadence specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 13725 — Steps to Increase Competition and Better Inform Consumers and Workers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must identify specific actions to address 'undue burdens' on competition via pro-competitive rulemaking and regulations, and provide semiannual reports to the National Economic Council on actions to promote greater competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent agencies are strongly encouraged to comply with the EO; agencies must identify actions and report progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 14154 — Unleashing American Energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall review existing regulations, orders, guidance, or other agency action to identify undue burdens on the identification, development, or use of domestic energy resources and work with OMB and NEC to implement plans to suspend, revise, or rescind unduly burdensome actions; eliminate delays in permitting procedures and identify agency actions imposing undue burdens on domestic mining and processing of non-fuel minerals for revision or rescission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs relevant Secretaries, Administrators, and Chairs to undertake efforts to eliminate permitting delays, including permitting by rule; does not apply to independent agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 14192 — Unleashing American Prosperity Through Deregulation (regulatory cap and offsets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes a regulatory cap for FY 2025 and directs that when an agency issues an NPRM it must identify at least 10 existing regulations to repeal; directs agency heads to ensure costs of new FY25 regulations are significantly less than zero (new incremental costs must be offset by eliminations of costs from at least 10 prior regulations). Agencies must submit annual regulatory costs to OMB and include each regulation in the Unified Regulatory Agenda; adding/removing regulations from the URA requires OMB Director approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a deregulatory directive requiring identification of multiple repeals for each new rule and centralized OMB oversight of regulatory agenda composition; does not apply to independent agencies (per the page 'No' in applicability column).

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 14215 — Ensuring Accountability for All Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs all executive departments and agencies, including independent agencies, to submit any proposed and final significant regulatory actions to OIRA before publication in the Federal Register; directs OMB Director to establish performance standards and management objectives for independent agency heads and permits OMB to review and adjust independent agencies' budgets so they align with Presidential policies; states President and Attorney General are to interpret the law for the executive branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires pre-publication submission of significant regulatory actions to OIRA, expands OMB performance oversight of independent agencies, and centralizes legal interpretation within the Executive Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 14219 — Ensuring Lawful Governance and Implementing the President’s DOGE Deregulatory Initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs agency heads to review regulations subject to their jurisdiction for consistency with law and current Administration policy; agencies must identify regulations that are unconstitutional, raise serious constitutional difficulties, are based on unlawful delegations, impose costs to private parties not outweighed by public benefit, or impose undue burdens on small business, and add those to the Unified Regulatory Agenda for modification or rescission in consultation with OIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs agencies to de-prioritize enforcement based on anything other than the best reading of a statute, continue OIRA review procedures outlined in EO 12866, and consult DOGE Team Leads on potential new regulations as soon as practicable. The EO aims to identify and schedule for change or removal regulations inconsistent with Administration policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 14270 — Zero-Based Regulatory Budgeting to Unleash American Energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs certain agency heads to incorporate sunset provisions into their energy-related regulations such that new covered regulations include a conditional sunset date not more than five years in the future, and requires insertion of conditional sunset dates effective no later than Sept. 30, 2025, into covered regulations; extensions require public comment on costs and benefits and may not extend more than five years into the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determining an extension or allowing expiration will not count toward deregulation requirements under EO 14192; the order does not apply to statutory regulatory permitting regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 14294 — Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs executive agencies to review and report to OMB criminal regulatory offenses enforceable by DOJ and any applicable mens rea requirement; agencies must post identified criminal regulatory offenses publicly and include a clear statement in NPRMs and Final Rules when a regulation contemplates criminal regulatory liability, specifying the relevant authorizing statute and mens rea requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any criminal regulatory offense that contemplates strict liability should be designated a 'significant regulatory action' for OIRA review under EO 12866. The Attorney General is directed to develop factors and publish guidance for agencies deciding whether to refer alleged violations to DOJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: EO 14295 — Increasing Efficiency at the Office of the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Directs the Archivist of the United States and the Government Publishing Office to reduce Federal Register publication delays by modernizing computer systems and eliminating unnecessary bureaucracy; requires reports on publication times to OMB and review of publication fee schedules to ensure fees are based on cost of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to reduce publication delays and align fees to actual publication cost; agencies and the Federal Register must report progress to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA procedural and transparency requirements (general practice arising from EO 12866 and related memoranda)
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA must regularize how it receives outside communications concerning agency rules under review; only the Administrator or designee may receive such communications, OIRA must forward communications to the agency within ten days, invite agency officials to meetings with outsiders, maintain a public log of contacts, and make available all documents exchanged with the agency at the end of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA issues return letters, review letters, and prompt letters (publicly posted) to communicate decisions, suggestions, or requests to agencies. Agencies should make available to the public all submissions to OIRA and identify changes made in the rule, noting those made at OIRA's behest.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-4 and Regulatory Analysis Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-4 provides government-wide guidance on the development of regulatory analyses, including how to conduct cost-benefit analysis and present alternative regulatory approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circular A-4 (2003 revision and subsequent updates/draft revisions) sets out procedures for benefit-cost analysis, discounting, and presentation of analytical results required for significant/economically significant rules when submitted to OIRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Peer Review and Good Guidance Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB's Peer Review Bulletin requires peer review of influential regulatory information the agency intends to disseminate; OMB's Bulletin on Good Guidance Practices (2007) establishes government-wide practices for agency guidance documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review rules and good guidance practices affect when and how agencies subject scientific or influential information to external review and how agencies develop, publish, and treat guidance documents that effectively bind the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective Review / Regulatory Lookback (cross-cutting requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are repeatedly instructed across multiple EOs (e.g., EO 13563, EO 13579, EO 13610) to develop plans for, conduct, and report on retrospective review of existing significant regulations to identify rules that are outmoded, ineffective, insufficient, or excessively burdensome and to make them more effective or less burdensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must institutionalize periodic reviews, report progress (timelines and accomplishments), make reports public, and consider public participation in lookback processes; independent agencies are encouraged to publish analyses and develop review plans within specified timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Planning and Unified Agenda requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must prepare annual Regulatory Plans and semiannual Unified Agenda entries listing proposed, pending, and completed regulatory and deregulatory actions; plans must include determinations on which existing rules will be reviewed and preliminary estimates of anticipated costs and benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory Plans must be approved by the agency head and forwarded to OIRA by specified dates; the Unified Agenda is published to inform Congress and the public of agency regulatory programs and planned reviews.
